significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that the same stored fact is "retrieved through partially different internal circuits depending on the surface form" and that a "small set of query-form-specific attention heads" predict and causally control recall; this is primarily a form-(ii) causal claim, with a predictive coupling, about one behavior. It would establish both the phenomenon of form-dependent recall and a compact routing mechanism, constraining explanations of paraphrase inconsistency documented by Jiang et al. (2020) and Elazar et al. (2021), while extending the MLP-enrichment/attention-extraction account used by Geva et al. (2023) to specify where cross-form failures arise. True and false are distinguishable: a negative result would rule out the compact router-head account, although it would not rule out distributed query-dependent retrieval or the broader storage-versus-access distinction. The topic-substitution check does not preserve the score: the topic alone suggests query-dependent access at the median, while the extra credit comes specifically from the selective causal routers and their predicted activation-recall coupling; nevertheless, because all consequences remain bounded to factual recall, this stays in the 5–6 band.

reach.justification: The named handles are the finding that router-head "activation predicts per-example success" and the "form-transfer intervention" that moves an answer-position retrieval direction from an easy form to a failing form. The activation signal is potentially ex ante because it is available while processing the query, before the answer is emitted, giving an auditor or inference system an opportunity to flag, reformat, or repair likely failures; the transfer intervention is narrower because it presupposes a successful alternate form of the same fact. After per-model re-extraction, the qualitative coupling between form-selective router activity and recall is predicted to survive, but the claim supplies neither fixed head identities nor a quantitative cross-model law, so much of the substantive handle must be recalibrated rather than directly transferred. The hypothesis is stated across LLMs and several query classes and could reach model auditors and deployment engineers, not only mechanistic-interpretability researchers; the topic-substitution check therefore fails to preserve this score because generic knowledge retrieval supplies neither this pre-answer predictor nor the corresponding repair knob.
